subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: When a signature-validated SMS callback exceeds the dispatch quota, should OpenClaw explicitly reject it with HTTP 429, or durably accept it for deferred delivery before returning HTTP 200?
rationale: HTTP success versus rejection defines the externally visible message-acceptance contract; code inspection cannot decide whether maintainers intend durable backpressure, explicit loss signaling, or intentional acknowledgement-and-drop behavior.

options.title: Preserve explicit rejection
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 and the existing retry/fallback signal until OpenClaw has a durable acceptance path for overloaded callbacks.

options.title: Add durable overload delivery
options.body: Persist validated callbacks in a bounded plugin-owned SQLite queue, acknowledge only after commit, and drain them with deduplication and recovery coverage.

options.title: Own acknowledgement-and-drop
options.body: Explicitly adopt HTTP 200 with intentional message loss and update operator documentation and telemetry to make that contract unmistakable.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit rejection
recommendation.body: Keep HTTP 429 and the existing retry/fallback signal until OpenClaw has a durable acceptance path for overloaded callbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate because their merged work established the current quota and response contract being changed.
